note: ADR-0500 withdrew the URL-in---database spelling, so the remote bundle must be accepted via --load (with --database a usage error naming --load), reusing the ADR-0496 fetch policy (.cl only, https, capped streaming staged scratch copy, safe-mode refusal, feature gate) and treating the fetched copy as scratch rather than a kept local store.

A query command already exists (ADR-0200), so extend it as a first-positional statement-session verb with -d/--database and shared help, keeping the live-clause behaviors (TTY shell per ADR-0231 replacing ADR-0200 §2 grammar, did-you-mean on usage errors, failure-progress reporting) intact.

Add the procedure with no database argument (ADR-0227 signatures acting on the session/USE database), gate it behind the CYPHERLITE_PREVIEW ontology feature, respect implicit/explicit transaction rules, list it in SHOW PROCEDURES, keep it always built, and do not rely on the removed system_ontologies graph surface.

Build on the tri-state re-arrival verdict (ADR-0516, superseding ADR-0478 §3) and the sparse generation-stamped tables with run-time ceiling (ADR-0521, superseding ADR-0478 §6), so any new re-arrival rule is budgeted, falls through to the DFS on Exhausted, and stays within the answer-shape gate.

Serve and the MCP server should take the single --read-only[=snapshot|live] flag (ADR-0480, which supersedes ADR-0306's --follow spelling and its Docker pass-through) while keeping ADR-0306's shared handle, post-verb-only usage error, no shutdown checkpoint, and the entrypoint execing `cypherlite serve` in the image.

The snapshot verb was removed in favor of `cypherlite clone SOURCE DEST` covering the dir/.cl matrix, so the plan should use or extend clone rather than add a snapshot command, keeping its new-destination, rollback-on-failure and read-only-source rules.
